# GTA VI Playthrough Tracker

> Free, single-page companion for Grand Theft Auto VI story mode: a per-chapter checklist of all 102 missions plus missable items, a money-making guide, an interactive map of Leonida (the game's state) with supercar spawns, hide spots and secrets, and reference lists of cheat codes and trophies. Progress is stored locally in the visitor's browser; no account, no tracking.

URL: https://runeball.no/GTAVI/
Source code (MIT): https://github.com/runeballe/GTAVI

## Sections (tabs on the page)

- [Checklist](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#checklist): 5 chapters, 102 required missions, finds, side jobs, missables flagged, plus all 65 Strangers & Freaks side missions grouped by contact; filter by open/done/missable; search.
- [100% Completion](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#hundred) (sub-tab of Checklist): all 35 in-game 100% requirements (gta.wiki) with counters; story and challenges rows fill in from the tracker.
- [Money Guide](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#money): money-making methods by chapter (e.g. Moses' garage car loop in chapter 2).
- [Live Map](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#map): Leaflet map on real in-game coordinates. Pin categories: supercars (13, e.g. Truffade Thrax — fastest car, garage code 8554013), chapter guide items, hide & money spots, secrets (UFO, tower egg), and ~1,200 gtadb.org landmarks.
- [Vehicles](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#vehicles): gallery of ~300 GTA VI vehicles by class (new vs returning, model year), with links to gta.wiki and to known spawns on the map.
- [Fastest Cars](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#fastest) (sub-tab of Vehicles): the 30 fastest cars ranked by the in-game Speed stat (no official mph/km/h exists), with location cues, how to get each one, security/tracker notes, map pins and a collected checklist. #1: Andrew Node's Thrax (9.2).
- [Bonus vehicles](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#bonus) (sub-tab of Vehicles): Ultimate Edition / pre-order bonus vehicles by chapter (Dinka Enduro, Dominator Buggy '67, Stanier '55, Shitzu Squalo, Cheetah '95…) with locations and pins.
- [Weapons](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#weapons): gallery of 74 GTA VI weapons by class, from melee to launchers.
- [Legendary Weapons](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#legendary) (sub-tab of Weapons): all 15 legendary weapon variants with locations, steps, map pins and a found checklist.
- [Easter Eggs](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#eggs): 14 easter eggs and secrets (Skunk Ape, UFO abduction, Dexter's apartment, Paul Walker's Eclipse, Arthur Morgan's hat, Cool Dog…) with where to find them, map pins and a found checklist.
- [MasterOfKnowledge](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#knowledge): lore and little-known mechanics — the 2021 San Andreas house photo found in Belville, the Manifest Canyon monument, pushing/flipping vehicles, Focus Mode encounters, 24/7 shops.
- [Door & safe codes](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#doors) (sub-tab of Codes): keypad codes for doors, garages and safes (e.g. Brian's Lock Up 7700, La Cascara Motel safe 6969), copy buttons and map links.
- [Codes](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#cheats): all 61 story-mode cheats with unlock conditions; 21 known d-pad codes, cross-checked across sources. Unlock checklist with progress counter. Enter on the phone: hold LB + press RB (Xbox) or L1 + R1 (PS5).
- [Challenges](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#challenges) (sub-tab of Cheats): all 80 challenges in 8 categories with a checklist; shows which vehicle cheat unlocks at 5 and 10 per category, and Platinum progress (70/80).
- [Trophies](https://runeball.no/GTAVI/#trophies): 55 trophies / 1,000 Gamerscore with descriptions; tick off as earned.

## Data sources

- Map tiles and landmark coordinates: gtadb.org contributors (CC BY 4.0) — https://gtadb.org
- Cheats and trophies: leonidaverse.com codex (unofficial fan wiki), cross-checked with gta.wiki and launch-week cheat guides
- Vehicles and weapons: gta.wiki (Vehicles_in_GTA_VI, Weapons_in_GTA_VI)
- Guide tips: community sources (Reddit, X, Skycoach, G2A, Insider Gaming, VICE, Space4Games, Rock Paper Shotgun)

## Notes

- Unofficial fan project; not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive.
- Some guide texts use older GTA V-era area names (e.g. "Vespucci"); those map pins are approximate.
